note: Quantities are per portion. Method steps are written for a batch: multiply by the portion count shown on the Cook screen. Protein is computed from ingredients.

items.name: Eggs on toast
method: Cook fresh each morning: 3 eggs scrambled or fried in a little butter, 2 slices toast.
Half an avocado on top when there's one in the fridge.
items.notes: Not a batch recipe. 8 minutes, one pan.

items.name: Skyr protein bowl
method: Stir a scoop of powder into 250g skyr, top with frozen fruit and a drizzle of honey.
Frozen fruit thaws in the bowl in 10 minutes, or overnight in the fridge.
items.notes: No cooking. Assemble the night before for a grab-and-go.

items.name: Bang bang crispy rice chicken salad
method: Dressing: whisk skyr, sriracha and sweet chilli. Set half aside for serving.
Dice the chicken, toss with paprika, chilli powder and half the dressing. Bake at 200°C fan (or air-fry) 20 minutes.
Cook the rice, toss with soy and sesame oil, spread on a tray and bake alongside 20–25 minutes, turning once, until crisp.
Tub: chicken and rice in the tub, diced cucumber and the reserved dressing in a small pot on top. Combine when eating.
items.notes: Cold lunch for uni. Keep the cucumber and dressing separate so the rice stays crisp. Skyr replaces mayo; edamame and avocado dropped for cost, add an avocado quarter when one's going spare.

items.name: Soy sesame chicken rice box
method: Marinate diced chicken in soy, garlic paste and sesame oil (10 minutes is enough). Air-fry 200°C 14 minutes or pan-fry.
Cook the rice. Tub rice then chicken.
Small pot: skyr mixed with sriracha. Cucumber sliced on top or in the pot.
items.notes: Eat cold or microwave 2 minutes. Freezes fine without the cucumber and sauce pot.

items.name: Spicy cucumber noodle salad with crispy beef
method: Fry the mince hard in a dry pan until browned and crispy, breaking it up. Add garlic paste, soy, honey, chilli powder for the last minute.
Soak or boil the rice noodles per the pack, drain, rinse cold, toss with sesame oil and a splash of soy.
Tub noodles, beef on top, sliced cucumber and sriracha in a pot to add when eating.
items.notes: Cold lunch. The original recipe is app-gated; this is rebuilt from the caption's macros.

items.name: Tuna pasta, cottage cheese tomato sauce
method: Boil the penne.
Blend chopped tomatoes, cottage cheese, purée, garlic paste and paprika until smooth; warm through in the pasta pan.
Stir in drained tuna and the pasta. Tub, cheese grated on top.
items.notes: The cottage cheese trick from the buffalo pasta reel: creamy sauce, extra protein, no cream. Good cold.

items.name: Peanut butter chicken wrap
method: Sauce: loosen peanut butter with soy, sriracha, honey and a splash of hot water until it drips off a spoon.
Air-fry or pan-fry sliced chicken, toss in half the sauce.
Wrap: chicken, cucumber ribbons, rest of the sauce. Roll tight in foil.
items.notes: Cold lunch. Make the morning of, or the night before at most.

items.name: Jacket sweet potato, tuna and cheese
method: Prick the sweet potatoes, air-fry 200°C 40 minutes or oven 220°C 50 minutes.
Mix drained tuna with skyr and sriracha.
Tub the potato whole; tuna mix in with it. Cheese on top when reheating.
items.notes: Reheat 3 minutes in the microwave. Not for the freezer.

items.name: Egg fried rice
method: Best with cold cooked rice. Fry the veg with garlic paste, push aside, scramble the eggs, add rice and soy, fry hard for 3 minutes.
Freeze the tubs the same day unless eating tomorrow.
items.notes: Add a tin of tuna per portion for a 50g-protein lunch.

items.name: Chilli con carne
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Brown the mince in a dry pan, add garlic paste, then cumin, paprika and chilli powder for a minute.
Add chopped tomatoes, purée, drained beans, crumbled stock cube and a splash of water. Simmer 25 minutes with the lid off until thick.
Cook the rice separately. Tub rice on one side, chilli on the other. Cheese on top when eating.
items.notes: Freezes for 3 months. Leftover chilli plus corn tortillas and cheese makes enchiladas. The reel's recipe is DM-gated, so this is the standard.

items.name: Bolognese and penne
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Brown the mince, add garlic paste, then tomatoes, purée, stock cube and paprika. Simmer 30 minutes.
Boil the penne, drain, stir through the sauce so it doesn't dry out in the tub. Cheese on top when eating.
items.notes: Freezes for 3 months. Bulk it with 100g frozen mixed veg per portion if you want more volume.

items.name: Coconut chicken red curry
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Sear the diced chicken in a hot pan 3 minutes, set aside.
Fry the ginger-garlic paste, then the curry paste; fry 1 minute.
Stir in a third of the coconut milk until it bubbles, then the rest plus stock (cube in 100ml water per 4 portions), honey and soy (standing in for fish sauce and sugar).
Chicken and peppers back in; simmer 10 minutes uncovered.
Rice cooked separately. Tub rice and curry side by side.
items.notes: Thighs work and are cheaper per kg; breast keeps it leaner. Freeze the rice the same day.

items.name: Soy garlic honey chicken with rice and broccoli
method: Dice the chicken, fry in a hot pan until golden.
Add soy, honey, garlic paste, sriracha and a splash of water; bubble 2 minutes until it coats the chicken. Sesame oil off the heat.
Rice and steamed broccoli alongside. Tub all three.
items.notes: Fastest dinner on the list.

items.name: One-pan soy chicken coconut rice
method: Marinate the thighs in soy, garlic and ginger-garlic paste, honey.
Rinse the rice into the pan. Liquid ratio 1 cup rice : 1.5 cups fluid, the fluid being coconut milk topped up with water.
Lay the thighs on top, bring to the boil, lid on, simmer gently 18–20 minutes. Off the heat, rest 15 minutes with the lid on, then fluff.
Steam broccoli separately. Tub.
items.notes: One pot. Coconut rice: freeze what isn't eaten within 2 days.

items.name: KBBQ garlic chicken bowls
method: Marinade: garlic paste, ginger-garlic paste, sriracha, soy, honey (sriracha and honey stand in for gochujang).
Coat the thighs, lay on a tray, grill or air-fry at 220°C 12–15 minutes until charred at the edges. Slice.
Cucumber salad: diced cucumber, sesame oil, chilli powder, pinch of salt; keep in a pot.
Tub rice, chicken, salad pot on top.
items.notes: Breast works if thighs aren't on offer. Salad pot stays cold.

items.name: Satay chicken skewers
method: Sauce: whisk peanut butter, coconut milk, soy, honey, curry powder and chilli powder until smooth.
Coat chunks of chicken in a quarter of the sauce, air-fry 200°C 14 minutes or pan-fry.
Warm the rest of the sauce in a pan. Tub rice, chicken, sauce over. Cucumber in a pot.
items.notes: From the cook.withcourtney reel. Lime and fish sauce dropped for cost; skewers optional.

items.name: Buffalo chicken pasta
method: Blend cottage cheese with sriracha, garlic paste and a splash of stock until smooth.
Fry the chicken with paprika, set aside. Soften the peppers, add purée for a minute, then the blended sauce.
Add the dry penne and enough stock to cover; lid on, simmer until the pasta is cooked, topping up stock as needed.
Chicken back in. Tub.
items.notes: Sriracha replaces Frank's; the cream cheese from the reel is dropped.

items.name: Chicken fajitas
method: Slice the onion and fry it with the peppers.
Slice chicken, toss in seasoning, fry hard with the peppers.
Tub the filling. Wraps stay in the packet; cheese and a spoon of skyr when serving.
items.notes: Filling freezes. Assemble the wraps fresh: 2 minutes.

items.name: Chicken, sweet potato and broccoli
method: Cube the sweet potato, toss in oil and paprika, air-fry 200°C 20 minutes.
Chicken rubbed with paprika and garlic paste: air-fry 200°C 16 minutes, or oven 220°C 20 minutes.
Steam the broccoli. Tub all three.
items.notes: The training staple. Freezes.

items.name: Beef and sweet potato hash
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Cube and air-fry the sweet potato 200°C 20 minutes.
Brown the mince with peppers, garlic paste, paprika and cumin.
Fold the potato through. Tub.
items.notes: Freezes. Fried egg on top when eating at home.

items.name: Sambal satay chicken, coconut rice
method: Marinate the thighs in garlic paste, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, half the sriracha, soy, honey and a squeeze of lemon (sriracha and lemon stand in for sambal and lime). Longer is better; overnight if you can.
Coconut rice: rinse the rice, cook it in coconut milk topped up with water (1 cup rice : 1.5 cups fluid), lid on, low, 12–15 min, then rest 10 min.
Satay sauce: warm peanut butter, a splash of coconut milk, the rest of the sriracha, a little soy and honey until smooth and pourable.
Sear the thighs 3–4 min a side, then lower the heat until cooked through. Slice.
Tub rice, chicken, sauce over. Cucumber in a pot.
items.notes: From the foodie_mette reel. Lemongrass and lime dropped for cost.

items.name: Green goddess chicken & potato salad
method: Poach the chicken: cover with salted cold water, bring to a gentle simmer, turn off the heat, lid on, leave 15 min. Rest, then pull apart.
Boil the baby potatoes 12–15 min until tender, drain, let them steam dry.
Green goddess: blend parsley, avocado, skyr, garlic paste and lemon juice with a splash of water until smooth. Season well.
Crisp the 'nduja in a dry pan until it breaks down and the fat renders.
Toss warm potatoes and chicken through the dressing. Tub. 'Nduja and its oil over the top when serving.
items.notes: From the erickbadgr reel, cheapened: tarragon, chives and anchovies dropped, skyr for Greek yoghurt. The 'nduja is most of the cost; leave it out and it's a £2 lunch.

items.name: Crispy chicken & creamy pesto pasta
method: Bash the chicken thin. Three bowls: flour, beaten egg, breadcrumbs mixed with half the parmesan and the parsley. Coat each piece.
Fry in a little oil over medium-high until golden both sides and cooked through. Rest, slice.
Boil the penne; keep a mug of the pasta water.
Sauce: blend the cottage cheese (or skyr) with the pesto, garlic paste and a splash of pasta water until smooth. Warm it gently in the pasta pan; don't boil or it splits.
Toss the penne through, off the heat add lemon juice, pepper and the rest of the parmesan. Tub with the chicken on top.
items.notes: Cream and gnocchi swapped for cottage cheese and penne: same creamy hit, a third of the cost, and it freezes.

items.name: Beef chilli enchiladas
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Brown the mince, add garlic paste and the spices, then tomatoes, purée, drained beans and a crumbled stock cube. Simmer 20 minutes until thick.
Spoon the chilli down the middle of each wrap, roll, and lay seam-down in an oven dish. A little chopped tomato over the top, cheese over that.
Bake at 200°C for 15 minutes until the cheese is bubbling. Tub two per portion with a spoon of skyr.
Batch tip: the chilli is the same base as the chilli con carne. Make a double batch, half with rice, half rolled up.
items.notes: Same base as the chilli, rolled up and baked. Corn tortillas if you have a kit; flour wraps are cheaper and sold everywhere.

items.name: Chicken curry with rice (madras powder)
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Fry the ginger-garlic paste and curry powder in a little oil for 1 minute until it smells toasty.
Add diced chicken and colour it, then tomatoes, coconut milk, pepper strips and a crumbled stock cube. Simmer 20 minutes.
Rice cooked separately. Tub rice and curry side by side.
items.notes: A plain, mild chicken curry built on madras curry powder. About £1.80 a portion.

items.name: Chicken & red lentil curry
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Rinse the lentils. Fry ginger-garlic paste, curry powder and turmeric 1 minute, add diced thigh and brown.
Add lentils, tomatoes, coconut milk and 250ml stock per portion. Simmer 25 minutes, stirring, until the lentils collapse and it's thick. Add water if it catches.
Rice on the side, or eat it as a thick dhal on its own.
items.notes: Lentils stretch the meat: 45g protein for about £1.50 a portion and it freezes brilliantly.

items.name: Chicken meatballs in tomato sauce, penne
method: Mix the mince with breadcrumbs, egg, garlic paste, paprika, salt and pepper. Roll into balls (6 per portion). Brown in a pan or air-fry 200°C 10 minutes.
Sauce: tomatoes, purée, a crumbled stock cube, simmer 10 minutes. Drop the meatballs in for 10 more.
Boil the penne, stir through. Parmesan on top when eating.
items.notes: Chicken mince is the cheapest lean protein on the list at £2.49 a pack. Freezes.

items.name: Honey soy pork mince rice bowls
method: Fry the pork hard until crisp at the edges, breaking it up. Add garlic and ginger pastes for a minute, then soy, honey and sriracha; bubble until it coats.
Toss in pepper strips and broccoli for the last 3 minutes.
Serve on rice with a fried egg on top. Tub rice, pork and veg; fry the egg when eating if you can.
items.notes: 5% pork mince is the same price as chicken mince and works better with soy and honey. Sesame oil off the heat.

items.name: Chicken burrito bowl
method: Toss diced chicken in fajita seasoning, fry or air-fry until charred at the edges.
Rice cooked and cooled. Warm the beans with the chopped tomatoes and a pinch of the seasoning for a quick salsa.
Tub in layers: rice, beans and salsa, chicken, pepper strips. Cheese and a spoon of skyr with lemon juice on top when eating.
items.notes: Eats cold or hot, so it's a uni lunch. Fajita flavour without the wraps.

items.name: Beef & bean burritos
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Brown the mince with the seasoning, add beans, tomatoes and pepper, simmer 10 minutes until dry-ish.
Rice cooked. Lay a wrap out, rice then beef then cheese, fold the sides in and roll tight.
Wrap each in foil. Fridge 3 days, or freeze and microwave from frozen for 3 minutes.
items.notes: Freezer burritos: grab-and-go for about £1.85 each.

items.name: Tuna & egg rice bowl
method: Rice cooked and cooled. Boil the egg 7 minutes, peel, halve.
Tub: rice, drained tuna, egg, cucumber. Soy and sesame over the rice; mayo and sriracha in a pot to stir through when eating.
items.notes: No cooking beyond rice and an egg. Cold lunch, 51g protein, about £1.55.

items.name: Tuna melt toastie
method: Mix drained tuna with mayo and pepper. Pile onto bread, cheese on top, second slice.
Toast in a dry pan with a lid, or the air-fryer at 190°C 6 minutes, until the cheese melts.
Cucumber on the side. Best eaten straight away; the filling keeps 2 days in a tub for a cold sandwich at uni.
items.notes: Make the filling in a batch, toast fresh.

items.name: Lemon garlic chicken wraps with cucumber skyr
method: Marinate sliced chicken in lemon juice, garlic paste, paprika and a splash of oil; air-fry 200°C 12 minutes or pan-fry.
Grate a bit of cucumber into the skyr with a pinch of salt for a quick tzatziki; dice the rest.
Wrap: skyr, chicken, cucumber, pepper. Roll in foil.
items.notes: Cold uni lunch. Cheaper than the peanut butter wrap and lighter.

items.name: Egg & cheese breakfast wraps
method: Scramble the eggs with diced pepper. Lay on a wrap with cheese, roll, and toast the seam in the dry pan for a minute so it seals.
Make 4 at once, wrap in foil. Fridge 3 days or freezer; microwave 90 seconds from the fridge.
items.notes: A batchable breakfast so you're not cooking eggs every morning. 30g protein.

items.name: Cottage cheese protein pancakes
method: Blend eggs, cottage cheese, oats and half a banana until smooth. Rest 5 minutes.
Fry small pancakes in a little butter, 2 minutes a side. Honey over.
Batch: they keep 3 days in the fridge and reheat in a toaster or dry pan.
items.notes: Oats are only a binder here, so this isn't porridge. About 32g protein a stack.

items.name: Peanut butter banana skyr bowl
method: Stir the powder into the skyr, slice the banana over, peanut butter and honey on top.
items.notes: The fruit-free skyr bowl: bananas are 16p, so it's the cheapest breakfast in the app at 55g protein.

items.name: Banana with peanut butter
method: Slice, spread, eat.
items.notes: The 30p snack.

items.name: Skyr pot with honey
method: Spoon into a small tub, honey on top. Frozen fruit if there's some spare.
items.notes: 16g protein for about 55p.

items.name: Cottage cheese and cucumber
method: Half a tub of cottage cheese, cucumber sticks to dip, sriracha over.
items.notes: 17g protein, under 60p.

items.name: Two boiled eggs
method: Batch: boil the week's eggs 8 minutes, cool in cold water, keep in the shell in the fridge up to 5 days. Salt and pepper when eating.
items.notes: 13g protein for about 35p. The one snack worth batching.

items.name: Peanut butter on toast
method: Toast, spread.
items.notes: 12g protein, more of a carb hit for training days.

items.name: Protein shake
method: Scoop into a shaker with milk. Water if you're keeping calories down.
items.notes: 32g protein. Costs what your powder costs.

items.name: Cheese and cucumber wrap roll
method: Cheese and cucumber in a wrap, roll tight, slice into rounds.
items.notes: 12g protein, travels well.

items.name: Garlic butter chicken with rice and broccoli
method: Fry diced chicken until golden. Add butter, garlic paste and a squeeze of lemon for the last 2 minutes; toss until glossy.
Rice and steamed broccoli alongside. Parsley over.
items.notes: Plain, fast, high protein. Freezes.

items.name: Chicken pesto pasta
method: Boil the penne. Fry the chicken with the pepper strips.
Blend pesto and cottage cheese until smooth, stir through the drained pasta and chicken. Parmesan on top.
items.notes: Creamy pesto without cream: cottage cheese does the job and adds protein.

items.name: Sweet chilli chicken noodles
method: Soak the noodles per the pack. Fry the chicken with garlic paste, add peppers and broccoli for 3 minutes.
Sweet chilli and soy in, noodles in, toss for a minute.
items.notes: 20-minute stir-fry. Eats cold too.

items.name: Beef and broccoli rice bowls
method: Brown the mince hard, add garlic and ginger pastes, then soy and honey; bubble until sticky.
Steam the broccoli, fold through. Sesame oil off the heat. Rice alongside.
items.notes: Takeaway-style, 40g+ protein, freezes.

items.name: Chicken and broccoli pasta bake
method: Boil the penne 2 minutes short. Fry the chicken with garlic paste.
Blend cottage cheese with the tomatoes. Mix everything with the broccoli in a dish, cheese on top, bake 200°C 20 minutes.
items.notes: One dish, four tubs, freezes.

items.name: Egg, potato and pepper hash
method: Dice the onion and fry it with the peppers for the last 8 minutes.
Halve the baby potatoes, air-fry or roast with paprika and oil 20 minutes. Peppers in for the last 8.
Make wells, crack the eggs in, cheese over, back in until the whites set.
items.notes: Weekend breakfast or a lunch. Eat hot.

items.name: Spicy eggs in tomatoes with toast
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Soften the pepper, add garlic paste and spices, then the tomatoes. Simmer 8 minutes until thick.
Make wells, crack in the eggs, lid on 5 minutes until just set. Toast to mop up.
items.notes: Shakshuka, basically. Sauce batches and freezes; eggs go in fresh.

items.name: Chicken fried rice
method: Cold cooked rice works best. Fry the chicken, push aside, scramble the egg, add veg, rice and soy; fry hard 3 minutes.
Sesame oil off the heat. Freeze tubs the same day.
items.notes: The egg fried rice with proper protein in it.

items.name: Coconut red lentil dhal
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Fry the ginger-garlic paste and spices a minute. Add rinsed lentils, tomatoes, coconut milk and 300ml stock.
Simmer 25 minutes, stirring, until thick. Rice on the side.
items.notes: Meat-free, 30g protein, about 90p a portion. Freezes for months.

items.name: Yogurt tikka chicken with rice
method: Marinate the chicken in skyr, curry powder, paprika, garlic paste and lemon; overnight is best.
Air-fry 200°C 14 minutes or grill until charred. Rice and cucumber alongside, a spoon of skyr over.
items.notes: Skyr marinade keeps it lean and tender.

items.name: Bean and cheese quesadillas
method: Mash the drained beans with the seasoning and diced pepper. Spread on a wrap, cheese over, second wrap on top.
Dry-fry 3 minutes a side until crisp and melted. Cut into quarters, skyr to dip.
items.notes: Meat-free and about £1.10. Eats cold in a lunchbox.

items.name: Protein porridge
method: Cook the oats in milk 4 minutes. Off the heat, stir in the powder, banana sliced on top, honey.
items.notes: 35g protein breakfast for about 70p.

items.name: Greek chicken rice bowl
method: Chicken rubbed with garlic paste, lemon and oil; fry or air-fry.
Tub rice, chicken, diced cucumber. Skyr with lemon and parsley in a pot for the top.
items.notes: Cold uni lunch. Clean and light.

items.name: Sweet chilli pork meatballs with rice
method: Mix pork, breadcrumbs and egg; roll into balls, air-fry 200°C 12 minutes or pan-fry.
Warm sweet chilli and soy in a pan, toss the balls through. Rice and broccoli alongside.
items.notes: Cheap pork mince, sticky and quick. Freezes.

items.name: Tuna pasta salad
method: Boil the pasta, cool under the tap. Mix mayo, skyr and lemon; stir through with tuna, cucumber and pepper.
Grated cheddar on top when eating.
items.notes: Cold lunch, no reheating, 45g protein.

items.name: Satay chicken noodles
method: Whisk peanut butter, coconut milk, soy, sriracha and honey with a splash of hot water.
Fry the chicken, add broccoli, then the sauce and soaked noodles; toss 2 minutes.
items.notes: The satay sauce on noodles instead of rice.

items.name: Egg and veg muffins
method: Whisk the eggs with diced pepper, squeezed-out spinach and cheese. Pour into a greased muffin tin, 3 per portion.
Bake 180°C 18 minutes. Fridge 4 days or freeze; microwave 60 seconds.
items.notes: Batch breakfast. Eat cold on the way to lectures.

items.name: Banana egg pancakes
method: Mash the banana, whisk in the eggs and oats. Fry small pancakes in a dry non-stick pan, 2 minutes a side.
Honey over. They keep 2 days and reheat in the toaster.
items.notes: Three ingredients, 20g protein, about 50p.

items.name: Breakfast burrito
method: Scramble the eggs, warm the beans. Lay on a wrap with cheese and sriracha, roll tight, toast the seam in the pan.
Wrap in foil. Freezes; microwave 90 seconds from frozen.
items.notes: 30g protein, portable, freezer-friendly.

items.name: Cottage cheese and tomato toast
method: Toast, cottage cheese spread thick, halved tomatoes on top, salt and pepper.
items.notes: No cooking. 24g protein for about 70p.

items.name: Peanut butter banana toast
method: Toast, spread, slice the banana over.
items.notes: Quick carb-heavy breakfast for training days.

items.name: Mushroom and cheese omelette
method: Fry the mushrooms in butter until browned. Pour over the beaten eggs, cheese on, fold when just set.
items.notes: Made fresh, 10 minutes.

items.name: Skyr with peanut butter and honey
method: Stir the peanut butter and honey through the skyr. Frozen fruit on top if there's some spare.
items.notes: No powder, no cooking, 31g protein.

items.name: Chicken pitta pockets with cucumber skyr
method: Chicken sliced, rubbed with paprika, garlic paste and lemon; fry or air-fry.
Grate a little cucumber into the skyr with salt. Stuff warm pittas with chicken, cucumber and the skyr.
items.notes: Cold lunch that travels. Two pittas, 45g protein.

items.name: Chicken and sweetcorn soup
method: Simmer diced chicken in 500ml stock with the ginger-garlic paste 10 minutes. Add rice and sweetcorn, 12 minutes more.
Off the heat, stir in a beaten egg in a thin stream. Soy to taste.
items.notes: Takeaway classic, about £1 a bowl. Freezes.

items.name: Creamy chicken and mushroom pasta
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Fry the chicken, then the mushrooms hard with garlic paste.
Blend the cottage cheese with a ladle of pasta water, stir through the drained pasta, chicken and mushrooms. Parmesan over.
items.notes: Creamy without cream.

items.name: Chicken, pea and lemon rice
method: Fry the chicken with garlic paste, add the rice and stock (1 cup rice : 1.5 cups), lid on 12 minutes.
Peas in for the last 3 minutes. Lemon and parmesan off the heat.
items.notes: One pot, freezes.

items.name: Chicken and chickpea curry
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Fry the ginger-garlic paste and curry powder, brown the chicken, add tomatoes, chickpeas and coconut milk. Simmer 20 minutes.
Spinach in for the last 3 minutes. Rice on the side.
items.notes: Chickpeas stretch the chicken: 45g protein for about £1.60.

items.name: Chicken and black bean rice bowl
method: Chicken tossed in fajita seasoning, fried with pepper strips. Rice cooked and cooled.
Tub rice, beans, sweetcorn, chicken. Skyr on top when eating.
items.notes: Eats cold. Mexican bowl without the wrap.

items.name: Lemon chicken with baby potatoes and peas
method: Halve the potatoes, roast or air-fry with oil 20 minutes. Chicken rubbed with garlic paste and lemon, in for the last 15.
Peas boiled 3 minutes. Tub.
items.notes: Plain and clean. Freezes.

items.name: Chicken and veg noodle stir-fry
method: Fry the chicken, add carrot ribbons, pepper and broccoli for 4 minutes.
Soy, honey, garlic and ginger in, then soaked noodles; toss 2 minutes.
items.notes: Three veg in one bowl.

items.name: Sticky honey soy thigh traybake
method: Sweet potato chunks on a tray with the thighs, honey, soy and garlic paste. Roast 200°C 30 minutes, broccoli in for the last 8.
items.notes: One tray, four tubs.

items.name: Chicken, spinach and tomato pasta
method: Fry the chicken with garlic paste, add halved tomatoes until they burst, then spinach until wilted.
Toss with the pasta and pesto.
Grated cheddar on top when eating.
items.notes: Fresh-tasting, 20 minutes.

items.name: Coconut chicken noodle soup
method: Fry the curry paste, add coconut milk and 300ml stock, simmer the chicken 10 minutes.
Mushrooms, noodles and spinach in for the last 4 minutes.
items.notes: Laksa-ish. Keep the noodles separate if freezing.

items.name: Shawarma-spiced chicken bowl
method: Thighs rubbed with cumin, paprika, turmeric, garlic paste and lemon; grill or air-fry until charred. Slice.
Tub rice, chicken, cucumber and tomatoes. Skyr with a pinch of garlic paste in a pot.
items.notes: Eats cold. Big flavour, cheap thighs.

items.name: Sweet chilli chicken wraps
method: Chicken fried and tossed in sweet chilli. Wrap with skyr, cucumber and grated carrot. Roll in foil.
items.notes: Cold lunch, 35g protein.

items.name: Turkey chilli with black beans
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Brown the turkey with garlic paste and spices, add pepper, tomatoes and beans. Simmer 25 minutes.
Rice alongside. Freezes.
items.notes: Leaner than beef chilli, same comfort.

items.name: Turkey burgers in pitta
method: Mix turkey, breadcrumbs, egg and paprika; shape two patties per portion. Fry or air-fry 12 minutes.
Into a pitta with tomatoes and skyr.
items.notes: Burgers without the bun cost.

items.name: Turkey and veg rice stir-fry
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Fry the turkey hard, add diced carrot, then peas, soy, honey and ginger-garlic paste.
Push aside, scramble an egg, fold in cooked rice.
items.notes: Everything in one pan.

items.name: Beef and rice stuffed peppers
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Brown the mince with garlic paste and cumin, stir in cooked rice and tomatoes.
Halve the peppers, fill, cheese on top, bake 190°C 25 minutes.
items.notes: Looks fancy, isn't.

items.name: Beef and sweet potato shepherd's pie
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Brown the mince, add diced carrot, tomatoes, stock and garlic paste; simmer 15 minutes, peas in at the end.
Boil and mash the sweet potato, spread on top, bake 200°C 20 minutes until the edges catch.
items.notes: Freezes in tubs. 45g protein.

items.name: Chilli-topped jacket sweet potato
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Quick chilli: brown the mince, add beans, tomatoes and spices, simmer 15 minutes.
Bake or air-fry the sweet potato. Split, chilli on, cheese and skyr.
items.notes: Uses half a chilli batch per jacket.

items.name: Pork and mushroom ragu with penne
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Brown the pork, add mushrooms until they colour, then tomatoes, garlic paste and paprika. Simmer 20 minutes.
Stir through the pasta. Parmesan over.
items.notes: Cheap pork mince, big ragu flavour. Freezes.

items.name: Chilli garlic chicken mince rice
method: Fry the mince hard with garlic paste until crisp, add pepper, then sriracha, soy and honey.
Rice alongside, fried egg on top.
items.notes: Thai basil-style without the basil.

items.name: Chicken burgers with sweet potato wedges
method: Mix the mince with breadcrumbs, egg, paprika and garlic paste; two patties per portion. Air-fry 200°C 12 minutes.
Wedges alongside, 20 minutes. Skyr to dip.
items.notes: Air-fryer dinner, 40g protein.

items.name: Pork and sweetcorn fried rice
method: Fry the pork with garlic paste until crisp, add sweetcorn and peas, push aside, scramble the egg, add cold rice and soy. Fry hard 3 minutes.
items.notes: Cold rice, hot pan. Freezes.

items.name: Turkey keema with peas and rice
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Fry ginger-garlic paste and curry powder, brown the turkey, add tomatoes and a splash of water. Simmer 15 minutes, peas in at the end.
items.notes: Dry curry, brilliant in a wrap the next day too.

items.name: Salmon, potato and broccoli traybake
method: Potatoes halved, oiled, roast 200°C 20 minutes. Salmon and broccoli on the tray with lemon and garlic paste, 12 more minutes.
items.notes: The dear one on the list, but omega-3 and 40g protein.

items.name: Salmon pesto pasta with peas
method: Bake or pan-fry the salmon, flake it. Boil the pasta, peas in for the last 3 minutes.
Stir pesto and cottage cheese through, then the salmon.
items.notes: Eats cold as a pasta salad.

items.name: Garlic chilli prawn noodles
method: Fry the pepper and broccoli 3 minutes, add prawns, garlic paste and sriracha for 2, then soaked noodles, soy and lemon.
items.notes: Ten minutes at the hob.

items.name: Prawn and egg fried rice
method: Fry the prawns with garlic paste, push aside, scramble the egg, add cold rice, peas and soy. Sesame oil off the heat.
items.notes: Freezes fine.

items.name: Tuna and sweetcorn pasta bake
method: Blend cottage cheese with the tomatoes. Mix with cooked pasta, tuna and sweetcorn in a dish, cheese on top, bake 200°C 20 minutes.
items.notes: The school-dinner one, 50g protein.

items.name: Tuna, chickpea and tomato salad with pitta
method: Everything in a tub: drained tuna and chickpeas, halved tomatoes, cucumber, lemon juice, oil, pepper. Pitta on the side.
items.notes: No cooking at all. 45g protein.

items.name: Prawn coconut curry
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Fry the curry paste with ginger-garlic paste, add coconut milk, simmer 5 minutes, prawns and spinach in for 4 more. Rice.
items.notes: Fifteen-minute curry.

items.name: Chickpea and spinach curry
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Fry the paste and curry powder, add tomatoes, chickpeas and coconut milk; simmer 15 minutes, spinach in at the end.
items.notes: Meat-free, about 90p, freezes for months.

items.name: Black bean and cheese burritos
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil first, then add the beans.
Warm the beans with the seasoning and sweetcorn, mash a little. Rice, beans, cheese in a wrap; roll and toast the seam.
Foil, then freezer. Microwave 3 minutes from frozen.
items.notes: Cheapest freezer lunch in the app.

items.name: Egg curry with rice
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Boil the eggs 8 minutes, peel, halve. Fry the paste and curry powder, add tomatoes and coconut milk, simmer 10 minutes, spinach in, eggs in to warm through.
items.notes: Cheap, quick, 30g protein.

items.name: Lentil bolognese
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Fry diced carrot and mushrooms, add garlic paste and paprika, then lentils, tomatoes and 250ml water. Simmer 25 minutes until thick.
Stir through the pasta, parmesan over.
items.notes: Meat-free bolognese, 35g protein, under £1.

items.name: Loaded sweet potato with cottage cheese and beans
method: Bake or air-fry the sweet potato 40 minutes. Split, warm beans and sweetcorn on top, cottage cheese, sriracha.
items.notes: Meat-free, 25g protein.

items.name: Cheesy bean pitta melts
method: Mash the beans with purée and paprika, spread inside the pittas with cheese, toast in a dry pan or air-fryer until melted.
items.notes: Ten minutes, under £1.

items.name: Peanut noodle bowl with egg
method: Whisk peanut butter with soy, sriracha, lemon and hot water. Toss with soaked noodles, carrot ribbons, pepper and cucumber. Boiled eggs halved on top.
items.notes: Cold lunch, meat-free, 25g protein.

items.name: Creamy mushroom and spinach pasta
method: Fry the mushrooms hard with garlic paste, add spinach until wilted. Blend the cottage cheese with pasta water, stir everything through the pasta.
items.notes: Meat-free but 30g protein.

items.name: Three-bean chilli
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Fry the pepper with garlic paste and spices, add tomatoes and all the beans, simmer 20 minutes. Rice.
items.notes: Meat-free, 25g protein, about 80p. Freezes.

items.name: Carrot and red lentil soup with pitta
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Fry diced carrot with the paste and cumin, add lentils and 500ml stock. Simmer 20 minutes, blend. Pitta to dip.
items.notes: Under 70p a bowl. Freezes.

items.name: Chicken, carrot and pea soup
method: Dice the onion and soften it in a little oil for 5 minutes before anything else goes in the pan.
Simmer diced chicken, carrot and potato in 500ml stock 15 minutes, peas in for 3. Season well.
items.notes: Proper soup, 30g protein.

items.name: Quick hummus with carrot sticks
method: Blend the chickpeas with lemon, garlic paste, oil and a splash of water. Carrot sticks to dip.
items.notes: 8g protein, fibre, about 45p.

items.name: Egg mayo half pitta
method: Chop a boiled egg into mayo, stuff half a pitta.
items.notes: 9g protein, 30p.

items.name: Tuna and sweetcorn pot
method: Mix. Eat from the tub.
items.notes: 26g protein for about 80p.

items.name: Skyr with peanut butter
method: Stir the peanut butter through.
items.notes: 20g protein, under 60p.

items.name: Avocado and egg on toast
method: Mash the avocado on toast, fried or boiled egg on top.
items.notes: 11g protein and good fats.

items.name: Protein bar (shop-bought)
method: Straight from the packet — nothing to make.
items.notes: Grab-and-go. Aldi's Harvest Morn bars are the cheap ones.

items.name: High-protein yogurt pot
method: Straight from the packet — nothing to make.
items.notes: 20g protein for under a pound at Aldi.

items.name: Beef jerky
method: Straight from the packet — nothing to make.
items.notes: Dear per gram but 12g protein in a pocket-sized bag.

items.name: Ready-made protein shake
method: Straight from the packet — nothing to make.
items.notes: 25g protein, no blender. Cheapest at Sainsbury's.

items.name: Babybel and an apple
method: Straight from the packet — nothing to make.
items.notes: Two mini cheeses and an apple.

items.name: Handful of mixed nuts
method: Straight from the packet — nothing to make.
items.notes: 30g is a handful. Calorie-dense, good on training days.
